questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose Milan for its vibrant city life, endless things to do, and easy access to other destinations.
I’d also heard so much about the amazing study-life there, which really drew me in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy; all the information I needed was somewhat clear and accessible right from the start

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No asstistance was needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find off-campus housing; Airbnb and Spotahome had great options, but I ended up finding my place through a Facebook group

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus in Milan was a great experience and gave me lots of freedom, but it can be quite expensive. I’m not sure if on-campus housing is even an option, as I didn’t meet anyone who lived there

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was relatively easy; within the first few days I went to the administration, and they enrolled me quickly. After that, I could choose my courses, and it was simple to get an overview of available classes, schedules, and exam dates

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think just overall and general questions. I found Massimo and the Erasmus administration really helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the course descriptions carefully. I would recommend reviewing the course descriptions, credit distribution, schedules, and exam formats/timings, and making your choices based on an overall assessment.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was actually unsure about the level since there was a wide age range among the students, but I would say it was probably at the MA level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at my host institution was very different from UCPH. At UCPH, there’s more dialogue between teachers and students, while at UNIMIA, it was mostly the lecturer speaking in a traditional lecture format, with less back-and-forth. Also, many courses had mid-terms, and attendance counted towards the final grade, which is quite different from what I’m used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Contract Law, Cultural Diversity and Human Rights Law, International Criminal Law, Space Law and International Organizations and Sustainable Development.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Comparative Contract Law, primarily because I had a really good and cool professor. Also I liked the exam form (multiple choice). Also, I really enjoyed Space Law.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation was really inexpensive and it was also fairly inexpensive to eat out on the local restaurants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many student associations that organized a variety of social events at different clubs and bars, which students could join and enjoy.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: We had very much fun on some of the social events at the bars, meeting more people from other countries.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We took a lot of trips around the north of Italy (Como Lake, Tuscany, Verona, Torino, Bologna, Genova, Santa Margharita, Sicily and many other day-trips)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it really easy, as the locals were very sweet and open-minded

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find any cultural differences particularly challenging, but I did notice some everyday routine differences that caught my attention. Italy is also a country with strong opinions on many things, but I quickly learned how they do things there

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language, the working-hours (including coffee-breaks and aperitivi)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a great spot to live (preferably close to the city center, and if possible close to the other students). Save as much as you can financially so you don’t have to compromise on activities or experiences while abroad. Just enjoy yourself and 6 months out of your normal routines with great weather, no work besides school, and a lot of nice and sweet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont have anything specific to add onto here.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Besides learning a lot, both in school and about the culture, I did really appreciate all the new people I have met during my time abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language barrier and learning the school system

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
